correctness.rationale: Exact spectral calculus gives covariance as q_minus I + (q_plus-q_minus)P and a signed error equal to one fixed projector-probing error times a scalar ratio. Weighted-average comparison proves the high-to-low covariance ratio strictly descends from kappa to 1/kappa. A scalar derivative places the exact supremum at one endpoint and comparison proves the p=1/2 switch. A Boolean-cube bijection and P^2=P give the subGaussian mass bound; flat rank-one signs yield the binomial count exactly. A standalone checker executed 1,200 dense covariance comparisons, six exhaustive small sign enumerations and 20 endpoint checks; it returned VERIFY_OK. No infinite claim relies solely on the checker.

value.rationale: In covariance-guided iterative regularization, fixed probes are naturally reused across many prospective stopping indices. This theorem identifies the single iteration endpoint that governs worst relative diagonal probing error and yields a horizon-free probability guarantee; the exact binomial law supplies a natural finite-sample reliability benchmark. The half-leverage frontier is independent of step and condition number and is a structural distinction, not a textbook single-matrix concentration calculation.
